item.title: Prime Minister Carney speaks with President of Guyana Dr. Mohamed Irfaan Ali
item.description:
Today, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, spoke with the President of Guyana, Dr. Mohamed Irfaan Ali.

The Prime Minister and the President discussed deepening ties in trade and investment between the two countries. They also explored opportunities for increased cooperation, including through the Canada-Guyana Memorandum of Understanding with the Canadian Commercial Corporation.

Prime Minister Carney commended President Ali’s leadership on environmental protection and biodiversity conservation.

The Prime Minister and the President agreed to remain in close contact ahead of the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next month.

item.title: Prime Minister Carney speaks with President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy
item.description:
Today, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, spoke with the President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The Prime Minister expressed his condolences for the victims of Russia’s latest attacks on civilians and energy infrastructure.

The Prime Minister reaffirmed Canada’s unwavering support for Ukraine.

He underscored the urgent need for Russia to immediately cease its strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and respect the energy ceasefire.

The leaders agreed to remain in close contact.

item.title: Prime Minister Carney speaks with Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi
item.description:
Today, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, spoke with the Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi. 

The prime ministers welcomed the increased engagement between Canada and India over the past year, including in areas such as finance, defence and security, people-to-people ties, and artificial intelligence. They underscored the opportunity to build on this renewed momentum.

To that end, the leaders reaffirmed their commitment to conclude negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) at the earliest opportunity, supporting efforts to double two-way trade by 2030. They welcomed the historic Team Canada Trade Mission currently taking place in India, led by the Minister of International Trade, Maninder Sidhu, as well as a visit to New Delhi this week by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Anita Anand, to advance shared priorities, including trade, energy, and people-to-people ties.

The leaders also discussed the impacts of geopolitical instability for the Indo-Pacific region and the need for trusted partners in the areas of energy and agriculture. Prime Minister Carney thanked Prime Minister Modi for his leadership in seeking a peaceful resolution to Russia’s war on Ukraine.

The prime ministers welcomed the bilateral security dialogue that took place in India last week as part of ongoing security and law enforcement engagement at the National Security Advisor level.

The leaders agreed to remain in close contact ahead of Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Canada in December.

item.title: Statement by Prime Minister Carney on Thanksgiving
item.description:
“This weekend, Canadians are gathering with family and friends for Thanksgiving. It’s a chance to slow down, reflect, and give thanks. For what and who you value most in life.

As we gather, we give thanks for Canada – for the rights, freedoms, and opportunities we share. Across our provinces and territories, in communities large and small, we bring different histories, traditions, and perspectives. Canada’s founding insight is that unity is not uniformity, that our differences are strengths to nurture rather than risks to manage, and that our values serve as an unshakeable foundation.

This Thanksgiving comes at a consequential moment. The world has changed, and Canada faces threats to our economy, our security, and our sovereignty. Meeting these challenges takes a strong country – and Canada is strongest when we stand together.

We see that strength in Canadians supporting local businesses, buying Canadian, and looking out for their neighbours. We see it in people giving back to their communities and working to create a better future for their families. Together, these choices add up to something greater than any of us could achieve alone.

Generations of Canadians have built this country. This Thanksgiving, we give thanks for all they have passed on to us, for the care Canadians show one another, and for the future we are building together.

Happy Thanksgiving, Canada – from my family to yours.”

item.title: Prime Minister Carney speaks with President of the United States Donald J. Trump
item.description:
Today, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, spoke with the President of the United States, Donald J. Trump.

The Prime Minister thanked the President for his leadership toward securing an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia. He expressed Canada’s strong support for this agreement and reiterated President Zelenskyy’s call for Russia to uphold it. It is imperative that all attacks on energy infrastructure and civilians cease immediately. 

Canada will continue to join allies in supporting Ukraine’s defences and its citizens. And we will continue to maximise our exports of oil and diesel to the United States that yield well over a million barrels of diesel per day.

item.title: Prime Minister Carney speaks with President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy
item.description:
Today, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, spoke with the President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The Prime Minister offered his condolences for the victims of Russia’s latest atrocities and reaffirmed Canada’s solidarity with the people of Ukraine. Both leaders underscored the urgent need for Russia to immediately cease its strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.

The leaders discussed the new agreement between the United States and Russia to supply millions of tonnes of diesel to the United States. The Prime Minister was clear: this agreement is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada, and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe. It will provide additional revenue for Russia and help finance its illegal, unjustifiable war against Ukraine.

Canada has imposed over 3,500 sanctions in response to Russia’s violations of Ukraine’s sovereignty. During their conversation, Prime Minister Carney assured President Zelenskyy that Canada will maintain and, where effective, tighten sanctions to support efforts to secure a just and lasting peace in Ukraine.

The Prime Minister underscored Canada’s unwavering support for Ukraine – for its sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity. Since Russia’s unprovoked and unjustifiable full-scale invasion began, Canada has committed over $8.5 billion in military support and over $750 million for Ukraine’s recovery and reconstruction. Most recently, Prime Minister Carney welcomed President Zelenskyy to Canada, where the leaders announced $355 million to support Ukraine’s air defences. During today’s call, they discussed increasing coordination with allies to build on this support for Ukraine’s air defence.

Prime Minister Carney and President Zelenskyy agreed to remain in close contact.

item.title: Prime Minister Carney announces landmark investment to retrofit one million homes, cutting energy costs and emissions
item.description:
The world is changing rapidly. In response, a confident Canada is choosing to build. We are building major infrastructure projects – new ports, mines, highways, and clean energy corridors that will transform our economy and unlock billions of dollars in new investment. We are doubling our grid through our National Electricity Strategy, to harness Canada’s electricity advantage and provide more clean, reliable, and affordable power for Canadians.

Heating is one of the biggest expenses for Canadians during the winter months, and too often that money goes to the most expensive and least efficient ways to heat a home. Over seven million households in Canada still heat their homes with oil, propane, diesel, electric baseboards, or outdated furnaces. Our government is laser-focused on giving Canadians options to lower their energy costs. That’s why, as part of our National Electricity Strategy, we committed to help one million Canadian households make retrofits.

To that end, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, today announced a $2 billion investment to deliver one million home retrofits across Canada. These energy-efficient retrofits will lower heating costs for Canadians and reduce emissions.

First, we are launching a new National Heat Pump Rebate to help up to 820,000 households make the switch to more efficient electric heat pumps. We will do this by:

  • Lowering the up-front cost of purchasing an electric heat pump: Eligible below-median-income households will receive a rebate of up to $10,000 for the purchase of an electric heat pump. Other eligible households will receive $2,000. Both rebates can be combined with existing provincial programs to bring the cost down even further.
  • Providing help when it is needed most: Every year, about one million Canadian homes replace their heating system. More than 80% of the time, it is because the old system broke down without warning. This new program will confirm approval within 24 hours, and a heat pump can be installed as quickly as a furnace.

Heat pumps are more efficient, cleaner, and safer than oil and electric furnaces. They will save an average of $1,400 a year for households currently heating with oil or electrical boards.

Second, we are working with the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC) and the Canada Infrastructure Bank (CIB) to help apartment building owners retrofit 280,000 units over the next eight years. We will do this by:

  • Providing affordable financing for retrofits: Through its Multi-Unit Mortgage Loan Insurance product, CMHC will help retrofit up to 250,000 additional units. This CMHC product has already supported over 140,000 energy-efficient units to date.
  • Unlocking investment in apartment buildings: Through its Building Retrofits Initiative, the CIB will support apartment and multi-unit residential building owners to retrofit 30,000 units.
  • Supporting building owners every step of the way: To advance building retrofits, we are also renewing the Deep Retrofit Accelerator Initiative, which supports building owners through all stages of the retrofit process.

Combined, these measures will support one million home retrofits and reduce Canada’s emissions by over 25 megatonnes – the equivalent of taking nearly eight and a half million cars off our roads for one year.

Today’s announcement delivers on a core commitment of our National Electricity Strategy. It is part of our broader mission to build at speed and scale to double our energy infrastructure and build a strong Canada that is powered by clean, affordable, and reliable energy. A plan that, done right, lowers costs for Canadians and reduces emissions.

Quotes

“Canada strong starts in a warm home. Today, we are helping one million more Canadian households make energy efficient retrofits. We are lowering costs, reducing emissions, and building a stronger and more sustainable economy for all.”

The Rt. Hon. Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada

“Building a stronger Canada means making life more affordable for Canadians while cutting emissions and building a cleaner, more resilient economy. When we help families and homeowners make their homes more energy efficient, they use less energy, save more on their bills, and reduce the emissions that drive climate change. By taking full advantage of Canada’s clean electricity advantage, we can lower costs, cut pollution, and create a stronger economy for Canadians today and for generations to come.”

The Hon. Julie Aviva Dabrusin, Minister of the Environment, Climate Change and Nature

“Affordable housing is also about affordable energy bills. By supporting energy efficient retrofits in apartment buildings and multi-unit housing, we’re helping lower costs for Canadians, improve housing quality, and build more sustainable communities.”

The Hon. Gregor Robertson, Minister of Housing and Infrastructure and Minister responsible for Pacific Economic Development Canada

Quick facts

  • The National Heat Pump Rebate program will be available through an online portal, with no energy audits before or after installation. Approvals will be available within 24 hours, making it easier to get a replacement installed quickly when a system breaks without warning – which accounts for around 80% of replacements each year.
  • Today’s announcement builds on previous measures to support energy efficiency, including the Oil to Heat Pump Affordability program and the Canada Greener Homes Affordability program.
  • In May 2026, the Prime Minister launched Powering Canada Strong, Canada’s new national electricity strategy, which aims to double the capacity of Canada’s electricity grid by 2050 and supply clean, reliable, and affordable power across the country. The strategy also aims to connect Canada’s electricity grids, build the workforce needed for the electricity system of the future, and increase domestic production of the technologies and components needed to power it.
  • The strategy is expected to deliver up to $15 billion in total energy savings by 2050 and lower total energy costs for seven in 10 Canadian households.
  • Under the strategy, the Government of Canada committed to expanding support for energy-saving retrofits for up to one million households through financing, grants, and complementary measures, including by making it easier for Canadians to switch from more expensive heating sources to electric heat pumps.
  • Approximately 80% of Canada’s electricity is already generated from non-emitting sources. By expanding electrification across households, commercial buildings, transport, and industry, Canada has the potential to reduce economy-wide emissions by as much as five times current electricity-sector emissions.

item.title: Statement by Prime Minister Carney to congratulate Anne Carson on winning the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
item.description:
“I congratulate Canadian poet Anne Carson on being awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature – one of the world’s highest literary honours.

A poet, essayist, translator, and classicist, Ms. Carson has reimagined the classics with wit, imagination, and a style entirely her own. She has brought ancient stories to new audiences and transformed the way we think about literature.

Drawing on ancient traditions with bold imagination and originality, her work has inspired writers and captivated readers around the world. Her contributions have earned her numerous other distinctions, including two Griffin Poetry Prizes and her appointment as a Member of the Order of Canada.

This is an extraordinary achievement for Ms. Carson, and a proud moment for Canada.”
